name: Warji-Gala
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Decker et al. 2022 survey cited on Glottolog for Warji-Gala; no phonological description located.

tone_statements.citation: Garba, Mustapha Ibrahim, Takim Okongor & Maitama Suleman. 2025. A descriptive analysis of plural formation through reduplication process in the Warji language. KWASU International Journal of Arts and Science Education 2(2): 311-324. Malete: Department of Arts and Science Education, Kwara State University. ISSN 0795-820X (online).
tone_statements.quote: Warji, Hausa, Karekare, Goemai and Bade, which are in the West Chadic group, have systems with two-level tones. Although some languages typically have sets of words distinguished only by tone, such as the following Bole from (West) and Margi (Central) have three tone Systems (Blench 2006).Warji, like other Chadic languages, is a tonal language that comprises three dialects known as Kikyadai, Rumbuna (rumba) and Zari (Schuh 1998). [...] [p. 317:] Reduplicationisa common plural formation process, and it is very productive in the Warji language. The paper shows that low tones are marked differently from those of high tones.
tone_statements.locator: p. 312, section 'Background to the study', last paragraph before 'Literature Review'; and p. 318, opening lines of 'Data Analysis' (page footers 311 and 317 belong to the preceding pages)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1998. A Grammar of Miya (UCPL 130). Berkeley: University of California Press.
sources.note: Closest fully described North Bauchi relative; its tone/accent chapter is the comparative baseline and it draws in Sirzakwai comparisons (per Blench 2007: iii) -- useful only as a proxy, not a Warji statement.

sources.citation: Garba, Mustapha Ibrahim & Muhammad Auwal Tayyib. 2025. Modification as a method of pluralization in the Warji language. Integrity Journal of Arts and Humanities 6(4): 143-150. doi:10.31248/ijah2025.206
sources.note: Nothing on Warji stress. p. 144: 'Warji, like other Chadic languages, is a tonal language..' and groups Warji with Hausa etc. as having 'two-level tones' (second-hand, citing Blench 2006/Schuh 2017); p. 146: 'low tones are marked while the high tones are left unmarked' in their data. Morphology paper only.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken et al. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-010. Dallas: SIL International. 123 pp.
sources.note: Only modern SIL publication covering Warji and Gala (wordlists + survey); may contain a phonology/transcription note; open on sil.org but could not be reached by automated download and not in the Internet Archive.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007 (circulation draft; PDF created 15 Oct 2007). Wordlist of the Sirzakwai (Warji) language with Hausa and English equivalents. Cambridge: author ms., x+41 pp. (sec. 3 Phonology pp. iii-vi; 3.3 Tones p. vi).
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 3.3 'Tones' (p. vi): two level tones High and Low plus downstep, rising/falling rare; 'Only a few words in the present list are transcribed with tones'; p. 1 notes none of the underlying sources regularly mark tone. (The tone paragraph begins 'Fali appears to have..' -- an evident template slip for Sirzakwai.)

sources.citation: Skinner, Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' (AAL 4:5) for the whole North Bauchi group incl. Warji: 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' Wordlists are untoned.

sources.citation: UCLA African Languages site, 'The Miya language' page (Schuh legacy materials),https://aflang.humanities.ucla.edu/language-materials/chadic-languages/miya/
sources.note: Lists Warji among the nine North Bauchi languages and points to Skinner 1977 as the group's main documentation; no Warji phonology.
